error: Changing the object while comparing how hard a push or pull is gives a fair test.
shows: Confuses the cause being tested.
example: Use the big pram for the hard push, beside: the same pram, pushed gently and then harder
if_many: Day 3 warm-up, 5 minutes: two pairs of cards, same object and different object; children point to the fair pair. Seen again in the day 7 exit and end item 1: day 9 Return and repair takes it if it is the largest group, and repair cards cover the rest. A third or fewer: a two-minute small group at one lane.

error: Pulling cannot change an object's motion.
shows: Does not link a pull to motion.
example: A pull cannot make it go, beside: the drawer opened when the knob was pulled
if_many: Day 4 warm-up, 5 minutes: two pulled objects; children show the start with their hands. Day 9 repair: two pulls on the same box, shown with hands.

error: An object at rest starts moving without a touch in these tests.
shows: Leaves out the touch as a cause.
example: The cushion slid by itself, beside: the cushion moved when the hand touched it
if_many: Day 2 warm-up, 5 minutes: touch and no-touch cards; children sort them and say it moved when it was touched.

error: An object that is coming close changes another object's motion before touching it.
shows: Puts the cause before the touch.
example: They stopped before they touched, because they were close, beside: they stopped when they touched
if_many: Day 6 warm-up, 5 minutes: three order cards (come close, touch, changed); children put them in order. Day 9 repair for end items 2 and 5.

error: A try that does not match the guess must be thrown away.
shows: Treats the guess as the answer.
example: Throw away the try that was not what I guessed, beside: keep both tries and say what each shows
if_many: Day 7 warm-up, 5 minutes: repeat one matched pull with the teacher and keep both records. Day 9 repair for end item 6.

error: Testing which way a push goes needs a different object.
shows: Adds a change that does not belong in a direction test.
example: Use the small tray to test which way, beside: the same tray pushed from the side
if_many: Day 5 warm-up, 5 minutes: same ball, two ways, tape marks. Day 9 repair for end item 4.

error: Mornings are always cooler and afternoons are always warmer.
shows: Takes the two or three days seen as a rule for every day.
example: Afternoons are always warmer, beside: on these two days the afternoon was warmer; we have only seen two days
if_many: Warm-up, 5 minutes, day 12 (and day 13 after the day 12 exit): lay a class chart row where the afternoon was cooler or the same beside one where it was warmer; the class says it varies, so we check each day. If the class chart has no such row, say we have not seen every day yet and keep looking. Seen again in day 18 W2: day 19 Return and revise, 3 minutes shared by every letter, circles the contrary pair and says the claim again for all three.

error: A date is counted twice.
shows: Touches or slides one square two times and so names a larger number.
example: Five rainy days with one square touched twice, beside: touch each square once and slide it into the box
if_many: Warm-up, 5 minutes, day 14: five squares in a line; each child's partner slides a square into a box as it is counted; the last number says how many. The day 14 exit is repaired in day 15 Return and repair, 5 minutes, in pairs while a small group works on C. Day 18 W1b: day 19 Return and revise, 3 minutes shared, touches each square once and replaces the count.

error: Adding overlapping categories: a day that sits in two rows is two days.
shows: Counts the rows and not the dates.
example: Two days, because it is in two rows, beside: the same date square drawn in both rows is one day
if_many: Return and repair, 5 minutes, day 15: a small group puts the date square into both rows of the retained live-month sheet and says one day, two rows.

error: A forecast guarantees what will happen.
shows: Reads possible as certain.
example: A storm will come, the page said, beside: the page says storms are possible this afternoon, so we get ready
if_many: Return and repair, 6 minutes, day 16: put the word possible and the might-or-might-not picture beside the answer. Seen again in day 19 F2a: day 19 Return and revise, 3 minutes shared.

error: A forecast tells what already happened.
shows: Asks a forecast about the past.
example: The forecast tells what happened this morning, beside: it tells what may come later
if_many: Return and repair, 6 minutes, day 16 (shared with D): order three cards, what we saw, what the forecast says, what may come later. Seen again in day 19 X19a and F1: day 19 Return and revise, 3 minutes shared.

error: Getting ready waits until the danger comes.
shows: Puts the plan after the storm sign.
example: We get ready when thunder comes, beside: we get ready before, and go in when thunder comes
if_many: Return and revise, 3 minutes shared by every letter, day 19: move the indoor-play card before the storm card.

error: Every region has the same pattern.
shows: Sets aside the records that differ by place.
example: Denver and Seattle have the same storms, beside: Denver ten squares, Seattle none
if_many: Return and revise, 3 minutes shared by every letter, day 19: match the squares and replace the claim.

error: A tree is shelter when thunder is heard.
shows: Takes any cover for a safe place.
example: Stand under a tree, beside: go into the school building
if_many: Return and revise, 3 minutes shared by every letter, day 19: put the building in the response sequence. Unfinished repairs go to the chart retrieval on day 20.

error: Building should begin before finding out the wanted change.
shows: Skips gathering information.
example: Let's build it now, beside: first we say what we want
if_many: Day 21 Return and repair, 6 minutes shared with B: put the want picture before the idea picture on the strip, say the order, then try one. Seen again on day 25 and in the day 27 end items.

error: Naming a favorite tool defines the problem.
shows: Puts a solution where the wanted change belongs.
example: We need a stool, beside: we want to see the notice
if_many: Day 21 Return and repair, shared with A: swap the tool card for the want card and say the problem is what we want to be different.

error: A farther stopping place always shows a faster start.
shows: Confuses where the trip ended with how it began.
example: It went farther, so it went faster, beside: we watched both leave the line
if_many: Day 23 Return and repair, 5 minutes shared with E: two lanes, two pushes, watch the start, then lay the stopping dots beside it.

error: A nearby bumper turns the ball before it touches.
shows: Misses the touch as the cause.
example: The wall was close so it turned, beside: it turned where it touched
if_many: Day 25 Return and repair, 5 minutes: roll past a bumper with a gap, then into it; each child puts a finger on the touch.

error: A design's look shows that it worked, whatever the result.
shows: Ignores what the test was meant to show.
example: It looks strong so it worked, beside: the ball stopped short so it did not work
if_many: Day 23 Return and repair, shared with C: match each result picture to the want picture, yes or no.

error: One success shows a design will always work.
shows: Treats one try as proof.
example: It reached once so it always will, beside: three reached, one stopped short
if_many: Day 24 Return and repair, 5 minutes: lay the reached and missed pictures side by side and say sometimes.
